title: Kuku clocks Rs 1,484 Cr revenue and Rs 89 Cr PBT in FY26; spends Rs 1,100 Cr on marketing
summary:
Audio and video content platform Kuku FM’s parent Kuku Technologies saw its operating revenue surge more than six-fold in FY26, backed by Rs 1,105 crore in marketing and advertising spends. The IPO-bound company also turned profitable during the year, posting a profit before tax of Rs 88.6 crore.
Kuku Technologies’ revenue from operations ballooned to Rs 1,484.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 241.5 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Kuku FM offers audio content across genres such as business, self-help, personal finance, history, religion, entertainment and fitness. The company also operates Kuku TV, Guru and StoRizz, offering audio and video content primarily through subscription plans.
Subscription revenue remained its primary source of income, contributing Rs 1,475.4 crore, or over 99% of operating revenue in FY26. The firm also earned Rs 6.86 crore from its pay-per-piece model, where users purchase coins to unlock content, while advertising income stood at Rs 1.9 crore.
The company also earned Rs 26.2 crore in non-operating sources such as interests on bank deposits, which took its overall income to Rs 1,510.4 crore  during the fiscal year ending March 2026.
The hockey-stick growth came as Kuku scaled Kuku TV, its microdrama platform launched in 2024. The company currently produces more than 150 microdramas a month as it expands its content pipeline.
On the cost side, marketing and advertising remained Kuku’s largest expense at Rs 1,105 crore in FY26, nearly four times the Rs 284.8 crore spent in the previous fiscal year. Employee benefit expenses increased 24% to Rs 74.1 crore, which included Rs 18.5 crore ESOP cost.
IT expenses more than doubled to Rs 56.7 crore, while operational costs surged to Rs 96.25 crore from Rs 8.65 crore, and payment gateway charges increased to Rs 43.2 crore. Overall, Kuku’s total expenditure rose 3.5X to Rs 1,421.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 411 crore in FY25.
Kuku’s higher marketing spending supported its sharp revenue growth, helping the company absorb the rise in expenses and swing to a net profit of Rs 182.7 crore in FY26 from a loss of Rs 152.6 crore in FY25. Its profit before tax stood at Rs 88.6 crore, while a deferred tax benefit of Rs 98.1 crore boosted its bottom line.
Its EBITDA stood at Rs 82.9 crore with a margin of 5.6%, compared with an EBITDA loss of Rs 159.8 crore in FY25.

The company’s cash and bank balance also increased 2.5X to Rs 293 crore at the end of FY26, while current assets rose to Rs 746 crore.
Ahead of its proposed Rs 3,500 crore IPO, Kuku is also building a 1,000-member AI-led content production unit to scale its microdrama business. The company plans to use AI across writing, production, post-production, dubbing and localisation as it looks to increase content output while reducing production costs. The company said 60-70% of its content already uses AI tools at different stages of production. Kuku also spends over Rs 200 crore annually on content and works with a creator ecosystem of around 50,000 people.
Kuku’s next phase will depend on whether its microdrama bet can sustain the momentum beyond an initial surge in demand. The format faces challenges around the high cost of producing fresh, short-form content, retaining subscribers amid low switching costs, and maintaining engagement as audiences have a steady stream of competing content. Kuku’s push toward AI-led production could help improve the economics, but scaling output without diluting content quality will remain a key test as the company builds a larger content business.

title: Indian startups raise $2.9 Bn in Q3 2026 as EV, AI drive funding
summary:
Indian startups raised less than $3 billion in funding in Q3 2026, down from $3.5 billion in Q2 and $3.87 billion in Q1. The quarter saw fewer large funding rounds, with Simple Energy leading the pack with a $182 million raise. The round also made Simple Energy the third-largest funded Indian electric two-wheeler OEM. Physical AI startup SiMa.ai, which has deep Indian roots and a major research and development centre in Bengaluru, raised another $150 million. Emergent, River Mobility, Navi, Slice and Pixxel also secured more than $100 million each during the quarter.

Despite the decline in overall funding, early-stage deals crossed the $1 billion mark in Q3. The quarter also saw six startup listings, including NSE, Rentomojo, Molbio, Milky Mist, Leap India and Purple Style Labs. Six startups shut down operations during the quarter.
[Overview]
According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $2.9 billion in funding during the third quarter of 2026. This amount included 46 growth and late-stage deals totalling $1.89 billion, along with 194 early-stage deals worth $1.01 billion. Additionally, there were 26 undisclosed deals during the period.
[Q-o-Q and M-o-M trend]
Q3 2026 saw a modest recovery in startup funding compared to the same quarter last year. Total funding rose to $2.9 billion from $2.78 billion in Q3 2025, but remained below the $4 billion recorded in Q3 2024. September emerged as a strong month for funding, as startups raised more than $1 billion for the third time in 2026. February and June were the previous two months to cross the $1 billion mark, with each recording around $2 billion in funding. The September uptick helped Q3 close above the funding level recorded in the year-ago quarter.

[Top 15 growth-stage deals]
In Q3 2026, India’s top 15 growth and late-stage deals reflected strong investor interest in mobility, AI and fintech, along with bets across consumer and deeptech sectors. Simple Energy topped the list after raising $182 million in its Series C round, followed by physical AI startup SiMa.ai, which secured $150 million in Series C funding. AI startup Emergent raised $130 million, while electric two-wheeler maker River Mobility secured $120 million. Fintech firms Navi and Slice raised $100 million each, while electric mobility platform Yulu followed with $93 million. EV maker Ultraviolette raised $85 million, while AI startups Ema and Sarvam AI secured $77 million and $74 million, respectively. Wearable tech startup Ultrahuman raised $70 million, while The Pizza Bakery secured $56 million. Healthtech startup Nua raised $50 million, followed by Third Wave Coffee at $43 million and aerospace and defence company Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group at $40 million.

[Top 15 early-stage deals]
Early-stage activity remained strong in Q3 2026, led by Pixxel’s $100 million Series A and Airbound’s $37 million Series A. Yuma Energy followed with $35 million, while Centricity and InRisk Labs raised $30 million and $27 million, respectively. Most of the top deals fell in the $15–25 million range, reflecting steady investor interest in early-stage companies.

Spacetech, fintech, deeptech and mobility featured prominently among the top deals. Data centre startup CtrlS raised $25 million, while foodtech firm Arboreal Bioinnovations secured $24 million. Business Nextgen Finance and Runable raised $21.7 million and $21 million, respectively. NeoGeo, Nexedge Capital and QNu Labs raised $20 million each, while Gravity, Piston and Plaza rounded out the list at $15 million each.
[Mergers and acquisitions]
The Indian startup ecosystem saw 33 merger and acquisition transactions in Q3 2026, covering sectors such as fintech, healthtech, AI, edtech, spacetech and e-commerce. Some of the notable deals included Samara Capital’s $120 million acquisition of stakes in Associated Road Carriers and Calyx Container Terminal, ITC’s $65 million acquisition of Yoga Bar and Udaan’s $52 million acquisition of Swiggy’s supply chain platform Lynk. Aurum PropTech agreed to acquire Housing.com’s parent in a $46.2 million share swap deal, while Ananta Capital acquired a majority stake in Phitku for $10.6 million. PhysicsWallah also acquired a controlling stake in Sarrthi IAS for $7.5 million. The quarter also saw strategic deals such as InsuranceDekho’s merger with RenewBuy, Adobe’s acquisition of AI startup Rilo and GalaxEye’s acquisition of spacecraft engineering company StarOps.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru remained the leading startup hub in Q3 2026, accounting for 143 deals worth $2.1 billion, or 72.52% of total funding. Delhi NCR followed with 56 deals worth $296.76 million, while Mumbai recorded 31 deals worth $283.3 million. Pune and Hyderabad ranked next with 11 and seven deals, respectively.

AI led Q3 2026 funding activity with $635.3 million, followed by EV startups at $583 million. Fintech ranked third with $487.7 million, while e-commerce startups raised $222 million. Deeptech and healthtech followed with $123 million and $103 million, respectively.
[Series-wise deals]
Series C deals led Q3 2026 funding, with 11 rounds worth $887 million, accounting for 30.51% of total funding. Series A followed with 59 deals worth $689.17 million, while Series B deals raised $506.2 million across 19 rounds. Seed-stage startups recorded the highest deal count at 88, but raised $174.7 million during the quarter.

[Layoffs, shutdowns and departures]
Layoffs continued across Indian startups and the wider tech ecosystem in Q3 2026, as companies focused on cost optimisation and profitability. Even Healthcare saw the largest workforce reduction, with around 350 employees affected, followed by listed company Zomato, which laid off 270 employees. Uber India also cut around 250 jobs during the quarter.
The quarter also saw six startups shut down: The Ayurveda Co, SatvaKart, Dream Money, Klydo, PicSee and Medial.
Meanwhile, the startup ecosystem recorded 10 senior executive departures across roles such as CEO, CBO, co-founder, managing director and president. The quarter also saw 85 key hires across the ecosystem.
[Trends]
UPI MDR: The return of discussions around interchange or MDR on UPI could reshape the economics of digital payments, particularly for banks and fintech platforms.
Apple Pay enters UPI: Apple’s entry into India’s UPI ecosystem could add a new global player to the country’s digital payments market and increase competition among payment apps.
AceVector IPO: AceVector is set to become the second e-commerce marketplace after Meesho to tap the public markets, pointing to renewed IPO activity in the segment.
EV funding: EV funding rose to $583 million in Q3 2026, driven by major rounds raised by electric two-wheeler makers Simple Energy, River Mobility and Ultraviolette.
Microdrama heats up: Pocket FM re-entered the microdrama segment, while Flipkart recently made its entry. The space already includes Kuku TV, Quick TV, StoryTV and EloTV, while mainstream players such as Yash Raj Films and Sun TV Network have also announced plans to enter microdrama production.
[Conclusion]
Overall, Q3 2026 reflected a mixed quarter for the Indian startup ecosystem, with total funding remaining below the levels seen in the first half of the year despite a recovery from the year-ago quarter. Large rounds were concentrated in EV, AI and fintech, while early-stage funding remained resilient. At the same time, IPO activity, M&A transactions and developments across UPI, EVs and microdrama added to the quarter’s activity despite tighter funding conditions.

title: Teachmint revenue jumps 2.8X to Rs 205 Cr in FY26
summary:
Edtech startup Teachmint continued its strong growth in FY26, with its operating revenue crossing the Rs 200 crore mark. The company also narrowed its losses during the year.
According to the company's audited consolidated financial filings with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, the company’s operating revenue jumped 2.8X to Rs 205.3 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 74.2 crore in FY25.

The growth was largely led by demand for Teachmint X, its AI-powered connected classroom device.
Teachmint X combines an AI teaching assistant with a digital board. The platform helps teachers plan lessons, create quizzes and homework, and grade student submissions, all aligned with the curriculum and what has been taught in that classroom. It also connects teachers and students through a single platform for classroom planning, engagement, and tracking student progress.
The company said Teachmint X is gaining traction in international markets, including the Middle East, SAARC countries and Southeast Asia.
“Teachmint X is powering global classrooms. Its multilingual, regionally context-aware AI lets us serve every classroom the way it teaches and learns,” a company spokesperson said.
On the profitability front, Teachmint’s loss before share-based expenses fell 34.2% to Rs 28.9 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 43.9 crore in FY25. The company incurred share-based expenses of Rs 9.9 crore during the year.
The company also benefited from improved operating leverage. While its revenue grew nearly 2.8X, operating expenses, excluding the cost of goods sold, increased only 11.6% during FY26.
The company expects this operating leverage to improve further in FY27 as it continues to scale its business. Teachmint was reported as India's No. 1 interactive flat panel brand by market share for January–June 2026 by global market research firm DISCIEN. It also plans to expand its network across India and overseas markets while deepening the use of AI across teaching workflows.

title: IPV leads Rs 7 Cr seed round in cybersecurity startup Zaperon
summary:
Cybersecurity startup Zaperon has raised Rs 7 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV).
The fresh funds will be used to advance product capabilities, launch enterprise-grade AI security frameworks and expand its presence in India and the US, Zaperon said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2021 by Vineet Gupta and Sachin Aggarwal, Zaperon is a cybersecurity firm that builds products to protect enterprises from data breaches. It offers a platform-centric approach to enterprise security that allows organisations to secure their entire IT landscape through a single Zaperon console.
By bringing together identity security, data security and AI governance, Zaperon enables enterprises to control how users, applications and AI agents access and interact with sensitive data and cloud infrastructure. The platform aims to replace fragmented security controls with consistent, identity and context-aware policies across digital and AI environments.
According to market research, identity security and data security represent an estimated $16 billion global opportunity today, which is projected to reach $35 billion by 2030.
The Delhi-based startup’s enterprise client base spans banking and financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, technology and government sectors, where protecting sensitive data and controlling access to critical systems are key security and compliance requirements.
Indian cybersecurity startups raised $89 million across 17 funding rounds in H1 2026, nearly double the $47 million raised in H1 2025.
Recent deals include QNu Labs, which raised Rs 200 crore in a Series A1 round led by the National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest to scale its quantum-safe cybersecurity solutions; Mitigata, which secured $15 million in Series B funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners for its AI-powered cyber-resilience platform; and CloudSEK, which raised $10 million from Connecticut Innovations to expand its AI-driven cyber-intelligence platform.
Other startups such as Deep Algorithm Solutions, Equal, Protectt.ai and Astra Security have also raised funding in recent periods, reflecting activity across fraud prevention, identity management, mobile security and cloud penetration testing.

title: Niyo’s income jumps 78% to Rs 178 Cr in FY26
summary:
Travel fintech platform Niyo’s income grew 78% year-on-year to Rs 178 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 100 crore in FY25, according to the company’s press release.
The company also cut its losses by 58% to Rs 33 crore in FY26 from Rs 78 crore a year earlier. Niyo said the improvement came from better efficiency, including the use of AI in customer service, operations, marketing and product development.
Niyo’s operating expenses rose 20% to Rs 201 crore in FY26 from Rs 168 crore in FY25. Employee expenses increased 17% to Rs 92 crore from Rs 79 crore. According to Niyo, the increase in employee costs was mainly due to the expansion of Kanji Forex, which operates under Niyo’s own AD-II licence. 
Despite the higher spending, Niyo’s EBITDA loss nearly halved to Rs 32 crore in FY26 from Rs 77 crore in FY25, the press release added.
Niyo is also expanding beyond its core travel business. The company said its revenue is now coming from forex cash, remittances, flights, hotels, experiences, international eSIMs and insurance, among other services. It is also selling more forex and travel products to its existing customers.
The company has set up Finnew Global Solutions IFSC in GIFT City and received approval to operate as a Payment Service Provider under IFSCA rules.
Niyo CFO Gourav Kumar said the company is now focused on getting more value from its existing customers, improving efficiency and moving towards profitability. Niyo expects to maintain over 50% annual growth in the coming years and become EBITDA positive.
Niyo has raised over $160 million in funding to date, including a $100 million Series C round in 2022. Its investors include Accel, Lightrock, Prime Ventures, Horizon, Tencent, and others.

title: After CEO, COO elevations, OTPless elevates Manas Poddar as CBO
summary:
Bengaluru-based identity and access management startup OTPless has elevated early team member Manas Poddar as Chief Business Officer (CBO), as the company expands its authentication business into broader identity infrastructure.
As CBO, Poddar will oversee revenue, enterprise sales and strategic partnerships at the startup.
Poddar joined OTPless in 2023 as one of its earliest team members and has led the business vertical since. Before joining OTPless, he worked at BharatPe from 2020 to 2022, where he was part of the technical team involved in the PMC Bank revival and the groundwork for Unity Small Finance Bank.
The appointment comes shortly after OTPless elevated its cofounders Satyam Nathani and Tanmay Sagar as CEO and COO, respectively, on September 18. Nathani and Sagar co-founded OTPless in 2023 and had earlier worked as founding members at BharatPe.
OTPless claims to have scaled to more than 300 million authenticated users and Rs 36 crore in annualised revenue, representing 2.5X year on year growth. The 12 member startup has also been profitable for the past two quarters.
The company provides authentication and identity solutions to consumer businesses through technologies such as Silent Network Authentication, WhatsApp Authentication, Device Intelligence and Passkeys. Its platform authenticates more than 300 million users, with clients including Meesho, Zepto, Navi, PhysicsWallah, ShareChat, Shiprocket and ixigo.
OTPless has raised $6.5 million from investors including Venture Highway, White Venture, FJ Labs, SIDBI and Piper Serica.

title: Seeds Fincap raises Rs 100 Cr in Series B led by Michael & Susan Dell Foundation
summary:
Gurugram-based NBFC Seeds Fincap has raised more than Rs 100 crore ($10.4 million) in a Series B round led by Michael & Susan Dell Foundation. Existing investors Z47 and Lok Capital, along with Norinchukin Capital and Alteria Capital, also participated in the round.
Last year, Seeds Fincap raised Rs 50 crore ($5.5 million) in a round led by Z47 and Lok Capital. In July 2024, it raised over $8.5 million in a Series A round led by Lok Capital and Matrix Partners India, now Z47.
The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand into new markets and strengthen its branch network, technology and risk management capabilities. It is targeting Rs 1,000 crore in AUM by March 2027 while continuing to focus on credit assessment and portfolio quality.
Founded in 2021 by Subhash Chandra Acharya, Avishek Sarkar and Sumeet Dhall, Seeds Fincap provides credit to underserved individual and MSME borrowers. It offers loans ranging from Rs 50,000 to Rs 10 lakh and uses a cash flow based approach to assess borrowers.
Seeds Fincap closed FY25 and FY26 profitably and disbursed around Rs 620 crore in FY26. Its AUM stood at Rs 722 crore as of August 2026. The company has expanded to 164 branches and has more than 70,000 active members.
Seeds primarily serves nano enterprises and small businesses, where traditional credit assessment may not fully capture business cash flows. The company combines technology with field teams across sourcing, onboarding, credit assessment, documentation, collections and portfolio monitoring to provide loans to small business owners.

title: Unveilr AI raises pre-seed round from AJVC at Rs 16.7 Cr valuation
summary:
Mumbai based Unveilr AI has raised an undisclosed amount in a pre-seed round from Aviral Bhatnagar’s AJVC at a valuation of Rs 16.7 crore. 
The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its engineering team and develop additional capabilities for its AI agents. It also plans to grow its sales team and expand its customer base across India, the UAE and the US. 
Founded by Sanditya Srivastava, the startup helps B2B and consumer brands generate leads through Google and AI search platforms such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude.
Unveilr AI combines search engine optimisation (SEO) with Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO). Its AI agents track how brands appear across search engines, identify queries where competitors are recommended and analyse the sources used by AI platforms. Its team then works on content, technical changes and online authority to improve brand visibility.
The startup claims that its customers can start seeing results within the first month. For an Indian B2B legal services platform, Unveilr AI increased AI sourced traffic by around 4.7 times and leads by 5 times, along with an 80% increase in ChatGPT citations. For a D2C brand, organic search contributes around 27% of total revenue.
Launched in February 2026, Unveilr AI currently serves B2B and consumer brands across India, the UAE and the US. The company has a team comprising IIT alumni and SEO and AEO specialists.

title: Antler, Nikhil Kamath back healthtech startup Aignosis with Rs 4 Cr seed round
summary:
Jaipur based healthtech startup Aignosis has raised Rs 4 crore in a seed round led by Antler, Nikhil Kamath and angel investors including Varun Dua and IIMA Ventures. 
The firm plans to use the funding to expand its AI assisted autism and developmental screening platform across India.
Founded by Raksheet Jain and Divyansh Mangal, Aignosis raised its first round in 2024 from investors including Rajneesh Bhandari and Amit Jain. The startup has completed its CDSCO regulatory process and received Class B certification. It was also part of Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First 2025 cohort.
The brand’s screening system uses a standard laptop and webcam for children aged 16 months to nine years. A short video across nine stimulus modules is analysed using computer vision to assess behavioural signals such as gaze, response to name and reactions to facial expressions. The system generates a risk report indicating whether further clinical assessment may be required and does not provide a diagnosis.
It currently operates through a Clinic in Clinic model and is deployed across more than 20 government Primary Health Centres in Rajasthan. It has also partnered with Mankind Pharma, whose medical representatives are supporting screening camps with paediatricians across India. The company is starting operations with Apollo Shines across around 125 schools.
Aignosis claims to have completed more than 8,000 screenings so far and plans to conduct at least 1 lakh screenings by the end of FY27. 
It will expand into Punjab, NCR, Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Maharashtra, with the company focusing on building screening and referral access across government and private healthcare networks.

title: Former Elevation Capital investor Mayank Khanduja joins Bessemer Venture Partners as Partner
summary:
Bessemer Venture Partners has appointed Mayank Khanduja as Partner in its India practice, nearly nine months after he exited Elevation Capital following a 15 year stint.
Khanduja will be based out of Bessemer’s Bengaluru office and focus on early stage investments in India, partnering with founders from their first institutional round onwards.
Khanduja brings 15 years of venture investing experience across consumer tech, gaming, healthcare, AI and deeptech. During his stint at Elevation Capital, he backed startups including ShareChat, NoBroker, PlaySimple Games, Jeh Aerospace, MOC Cancer Care, Loop Health, Atlys, Seekho, General Autonomy and PierSight.
Before joining Elevation, Khanduja worked with McKinsey. 
“Mayank has spent 15 years partnering with founders at the earliest stages and helping them build enduring companies. His depth across consumer tech and AI strengthens our early stage practice in India,” said Vishal Gupta, Partner at Bessemer Venture Partners.
Khanduja said Bessemer’s research led approach and track record made it a strong platform to partner with founders from the early stages.
Bessemer has been investing in India for over two decades. Its portfolio includes Medi Assist, Perfios, Swiggy and Urban Company, among others. Its recent investments include Sarvam, Boldfit, Vetic, Easebuzz, Inrisk and Pluro.
In March 2025, Bessemer announced its second India fund with $350 million in capital, targeting sectors including AI, fintech, enterprise tech, health, consumer and cybersecurity. Globally, the firm recently raised $5.75 billion to invest across stages from seed to growth.

title: Bangalore Watch Company raises $1.4 Mn in seed round from customers, family office, HNIs
summary:
Indian luxury watch brand Bangalore Watch Company (BWC) has raised $1.4 million in a seed round from a group of its customers, including family office principals and high-net-worth individuals from India and overseas.
The fresh capital will be used to expand BWC’s presence in the global independent watch market. It also plans to focus on two to three strategic overseas locations in markets with established watch collector communities, along with potentially one additional location in India.
Founded in 2018 by Nirupesh Joshi and Mercy Amalraj, BWC makes mechanical watches in India and exports them to more than 30 countries. Its collections are based on themes such as aviation, space, cricket and the outdoors, with a focus on modern Indian stories.
The company currently operates a single flagship boutique in Bengaluru and sells watches priced between Rs 1.5 lakh and Rs 3 lakh. BWC has an annual production capacity of around 1,500 watches and plans to increase this fourfold over the next three to five years.
BWC has developed watches using materials such as recovered fighter-plane aluminium and aircraft carrier materials. 
It has also developed its own Cerasteel material and made a watch that qualified for spaceflight. The brand has participated in Dubai Watch Week 2025 and Geneva Watch Days 2026, while its watches have been listed for the GPHG Awards three times.

title: SBI Mutual Fund raises Swiggy stake above 5% after Rs 300 Cr share purchase
summary:
SBI Mutual Fund has increased its stake in food delivery and quick commerce major Swiggy to over 5% after acquiring an additional 1.18 crore shares through a market purchase on September 29.
The acquisition is valued at around Rs 300 crore, based on Swiggy’s closing price of Rs 253.70 on September 29. The filing, however, does not disclose the actual acquisition price.
According to a regulatory filing, SBI Mutual Fund, through its various schemes, acquired 1,18,38,465 shares, equivalent to a 0.4289% stake in Swiggy.
Before the transaction, SBI Mutual Fund held 12.97 crore shares, representing a 4.70% stake in the company. Following the purchase, its holding increased to 14.15 crore shares, or 5.12%.
The purchase took SBI Mutual Fund’s holding past the 5% threshold, triggering a disclosure under Regulation 29(1) of SEBI’s Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers Regulations.
SBI Funds Management submitted the disclosure to Swiggy, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and BSE on September 30.
The stake increase comes after Swiggy shareholders approved a 49.5% cap on aggregate foreign ownership at its AGM in August, clearing a key hurdle in its transition to an Indian-owned and controlled company (IOCC). Swiggy’s domestic ownership had crossed 50% in July, while foreign ownership stood at 49.76%.
In Q1 FY27, Swiggy reported 7% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue to Rs 6,812 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 4,961 crore in Q1 FY25. The company also narrowed its losses by 34% to Rs 791 crore during the period.
Swiggy’s shares were trading at around Rs 247 as of 10:40 AM on Thursday, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 68,125 crore ($7.17 billion).

title: Moneyview shares debut at 64% premium after 100X IPO subscription
summary:
Digital lending platform Moneyview made a strong debut on the stock exchanges on Thursday, with its shares listing at a premium of over 60% to the IPO price.
Moneyview shares opened at Rs 55.61 on the BSE, up 63.6% from the issue price of Rs 34. On the NSE, the stock opened at Rs 55, marking a 61.8% premium.
The strong debut comes days after the fintech’s Rs 1,092 crore IPO was subscribed 98.46 times on the final day of bidding. The issue received particularly strong demand from qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), whose portion was subscribed 227.45 times. The non-institutional investor portion was subscribed 115.41 times, while the retail portion saw 19.57X subscription.
Moneyview had fixed the IPO price band at Rs 32-34 per share, valuing the company at nearly Rs 6,000 crore at the upper end. The IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 750 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of 10.05 crore shares worth around Rs 342 crore.
Of the fresh capital, Moneyview plans to use Rs 325 crore to support its lending operations, while another Rs 250 crore will be invested in strengthening the capital base of its NBFC subsidiary, Whizdm Finance.
The company reported Rs 3,351 crore in revenue and Rs 242 crore in profit in FY26. Its loan disbursals rose 31% to Rs 23,099 crore during the year, while its assets under management stood at Rs 22,520 crore as of June 2026.
Founded in 2014 by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview offers personal loans and other financial products including insurance, digital gold, credit cards and UPI services.
With the stock opening at around Rs 55, Moneyview's market capitalisation has moved significantly above the valuation implied by its IPO price.

title: UPI transaction volume stays above 24 Bn despite 1.8% M-o-M dip in September
summary:
Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processed 24.07 billion transactions worth Rs 29.37 lakh crore in September 2026, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The September transaction volume declined 1.8% month-on-month (M-o-M) from the record 24.51 billion transactions processed in August. Transaction value also fell 1.5% from Rs 29.82 lakh crore in August.
The minor monthly dip was due to the difference in the number of days, with August having 31 days compared with 30 days in September. On a daily basis, UPI processed an average of 802 million transactions in September versus 791 million in August, a 1.4% increase. The average daily transaction value also rose to Rs 97,913 crore from Rs 96,205 crore in August.
On a year-on-year basis, UPI transaction volume grew 23%, while transaction value increased 18% in September.
UPI crossed the 23 billion monthly transaction mark for the first time in May 2026 with 23.2 billion transactions worth Rs 29.90 lakh crore. It then processed 23.66 billion transactions in July before reaching a record 24.51 billion transactions in August.
In August, PhonePe led the UPI market with a 45.64% share of transaction volume, followed by Google Pay at 32.26% and Paytm at 8.03%. The three apps together accounted for 85.93% of UPI transaction volume. NPCI is yet to release the app-wise breakup for September.
In value terms, PhonePe held a 47.82% share, followed by Google Pay at 33.78% and Paytm at 6.87% in August.
Meanwhile, the new UPI Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework will take effect from October 15 for specified person-to-merchant transactions above Rs 2,000. The framework provides for a 0.4% MDR, with a cap of Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. UPI payments up to Rs 2,000 and person-to-person transactions will remain outside the levy.

India’s electric two-wheeler market rebounded in September, with registrations rising over 12% month-on-month to 2.07 lakh units from 1.85 lakh units in August. TVS Motor retained its leadership, while legacy players, Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp recorded strong growth during the month.
According to the latest Vahan data, TVS Motor led the electric two-wheeler market with 53,989 registrations in September, accounting for a 26.06% market share. The company’s registrations increased 9.55% month on month from 49,284 units in August.

Bajaj Auto retained the second spot with 48,383 registrations and a 23.36% market share. Its registrations rose 17% month on month, with the company adding over 7,000 units compared to August.
Ather Energy ranked third with 30,479 registrations and a 14.71% market share. The company’s registrations in September grew nearly 5%  month-on-month compared to August, when it registered 29,068 units.
Hero MotoCorp recorded one of the strongest gains among the leading players, with registrations jumping 27% month on month to 24,306 units from 19,144 units in August. The company captured an 11.73% share of the market in September.
Ola Electric remained in fifth position with 13,449 registrations and a 6.49% market share. It was the only player among the top five to record a monthly decline, with registrations falling 3.53% from 13,941 units in August.
Greaves Electric Mobility followed with 9,316 registrations and a 4.5% market share, with registrations growing 8% month on month. River Mobility registered 5,549 units, a 6.4% gain from August, while BGauss remained largely flat with 5,023 registrations.
Among smaller players, Bounce Electric recorded a sharp increase, with registrations nearly tripling to 3,069 units from 1,049 units in August. E-Sprinto Green Energy also saw registrations surge to 1,997 units from just 120 units in the previous month.
Simple Energy, which recently raised $182 million in a Series C round, dropped out of the top 10 as its registrations fell nearly 19% to 1,351 units in September from 1,664 units in August.

Noida-based fintech PayMe has nearly doubled its monthly loan disbursals to more than Rs 200 crore in September 2026, as it scales its lending operations.
The RBI-registered NBFC had crossed Rs 100 crore in monthly disbursals earlier and reached Rs 120 crore in July 2026. The company is now targeting more than Rs 2,000 crore in annual disbursals in FY27.
Founded in 2016 by Mahesh Shukla, PayMe offers personal loans, salary advances and business loans to salaried professionals, gig workers and self-employed individuals. The company uses AI-based underwriting for its lending operations and disbursed more than Rs 1,300 crore in FY26.
PayMe operates as the customer-facing lending platform, while Scale Up is its RBI-registered NBFC. Credit Assist provides an AI-based platform focused on credit health, while Huey Tech develops the technology and underwriting infrastructure used across the group.
The company plans to raise its monthly disbursal run rate to Rs 500 crore by the end of FY27. PayMe is also preparing to launch an investment and mentorship show for technology startups from Uttar Pradesh, which will provide funding and mentorship to selected founders.
Meanwhile, PayMe is preparing for an IPO in the coming year. The company said the proposed listing will support its next phase of growth as it expands its lending business and technology platform.

title: EV startup Simple Energy raises $182 Mn in Series C round
summary:
Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler maker Simple Energy has raised Rs 1,750 crore ($182 million) in a Series C funding round. This is its largest fundraise to date and the third-largest funding by an Indian electric two-wheeler OEM, according to the company.
The fundraise was led by the family office of Dr Arokiaswamy Velumani, founder of Thyrocare Technologies, along with founder and CEO Suhas Rajkumar and co-founder and CFO Ankit Gupta. Bengaluru-based HNI Amit Mishra and the Haran Family Office also participated.
The entire capital was raised through equity. With this fundraise, Simple Energy’s total capital raised has crossed Rs 2,530 crore ($263 million).
The fresh capital will be used to set up a new manufacturing facility, increase production capacity, expand its distribution and service network, hire talent and fund research and development for its next product cycle. The company will also use the funds for marketing and supply chain operations.
Simple Energy currently has a production capacity of 10,000 units per month and operates more than 80 outlets across over 60 cities. Its product portfolio includes Simple One, Simple Wave and Simple Ultra electric scooters.
The company said its monthly sales have grown more than fourfold over the past year. It has launched Simple Wave and Simple Ultra in the past eight months for the family and performance scooter segments.
Simple Energy reported operating revenue of around Rs 150-160 crore in FY26, compared with about Rs 40 crore in FY25. This represents a nearly fourfold increase in revenue. The company currently derives most of its sales from southern states.
Simple Energy had raised Rs 250 crore through a mix of debt and equity in June 2026, following a $10 million all-equity bridge fundraise in September 2025. Before that, it raised $20 million in Series A funding in July 2024, more than $20 million in a bridge fundraise in February 2023 and $21 million in pre-Series A funding in November 2021.
Founded in 2019 by Suhas Rajkumar and Shreshth Mishra, Simple Energy later brought Ankit Gupta on board as a cofounder. The company develops electric two-wheelers and key components such as chassis, battery, motor and software in-house.
Simple Energy claims to be the first Indian OEM to commercially produce heavy rare-earth-free motors. It also claims to be the first Indian OEM to offer a lifetime warranty on its motor and battery.

title: Netmeds posts flat revenue at Rs 45 Cr in FY26; remains profitable
summary:
Reliance-backed Netmeds remained a relatively small player compared to online pharmacy rivals such as Tata 1mg and PharmEasy, with its operating revenue remaining largely flat in FY26. The company, however, stayed profitable with Rs 5.5 crore during the year.
Netmeds’ revenue from operations grew marginally by 2.3% in the fiscal year ended March 2026 to Rs 44.7 crore from Rs 43.7 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Netmeds operates an online healthcare platform that sells pharmaceutical and healthcare products and provides services across diagnostics, doctor consultations and other healthcare offerings. The company also generates revenue through marketing and healthcare-related services.
Income from services continued to account for the bulk of Netmeds’ revenue during FY26. Gross service income stood at Rs 46.3 crore compared with Rs 46.2 crore in FY25.
Revenue from the sale of goods, meanwhile, increased 24% to Rs 6.03 crore from Rs 4.86 crore in the previous fiscal year. After adjusting Rs 7.6 crore towards GST recovered, Netmeds’ revenue from operations stood at Rs 44.7 crore in FY26.
The company also generated Rs 3.24 crore from non-operating sources, which took its total income to Rs 47.94 crore during the year.
Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost centre for Netmeds, increasing 4% to Rs 13.7 crore in FY26 compared to Rs 13.2 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, technical service costs declined 12% to Rs 9.12 crore, whereas the cost of materials increased 12% to Rs 4.44 crore during the year.
Advertising and promotional expenditure surged 76% to Rs 2.9 crore from Rs 1.65 crore in FY25. Other overheads such as legal & professional rent stood added another Rs 12.24 crore, taking the company’s total expenditure to Rs 42.4 crore from Rs 41.6 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Despite its relatively modest topline growth, Netmeds remained profitable during FY26 with Rs 5.5 crore, which declined by 5% compared to FY25. Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at 4.5% and 5.66%, respectively.

The company spent around Rs 0.95 to earn a rupee of operating revenue during the year, unchanged from FY25.
Reliance Industries Limited, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Reliance Retail Ventures Limited (RRVL) has acquired a majority equity stake in Netmeds for about Rs 620 crore in cash in August 2020.
The platform competes with Tata 1mg, which reported Rs 2,936 crore in revenue and a consolidated loss of Rs 287 crore in FY26, while PharmEasy parent API Holdings posted Rs 6,869 crore in revenue during the year. Apollo 24/7 is another key player in India’s online healthcare and pharmacy market.

title: Longevity startup Vytalyou raises Rs 9 Cr in pre-Series A round
summary:
Doctor-led longevity and preventive healthcare startup Vytalyou has raised Rs 9 crore in a pre-Series A round from Chetan Jain of Pharma Dose and Ratan Jain of Venus Industries at a valuation of around Rs 33 crore.
The proceeds will be used to expand its network of Incremental Lifestyle Clinics in Mumbai, Vytalyou said in a press release.
Founded in 2025 by Chirantan Bose and Preetesh Bhandari, Vytalyou provides preventive healthcare and longevity-focused services, combining diagnostics with personalised health interventions and medically supervised care.
The Mumbai-based startup offers services across pathology, radiology, cardio-respiratory assessments, body composition evaluation, genetic and cancer screening, gut microbiome evaluation, personalised IV therapies and regenerative interventions. It also offers non-invasive pain management technologies for chronic musculoskeletal conditions.
Vytalyou uses an AI-based algorithm for its Predictive Longevity Evaluation, which assesses an individual’s health profile, biological ageing and potential health risks. Doctors review the assessment and develop a medically supervised care plan based on the findings.
The company said it has served close to 1,000 clients since opening its first centre, with around half coming through walk-ins and the rest through word-of-mouth referrals. It plans to expand to 10 locations across India in the coming years.
Vytalyou operates in India’s growing preventive healthcare and longevity segment, which has also seen startups such as Biopeak, Cent, Elevate Now and Decode Age raise capital.
Biopeak raised $2.7 million in follow-on funding in January this year, while Cent, co-founded by Practo’s Shashank ND, raised around $5 million for its AI-led early-detection platform covering cancer, cardiac, neurological and metabolic risks.
Elevate Now raised Rs 18 crore in a seed round, while Decode Age raised Rs 14.48 crore in a pre-Series A round to expand its longevity research, biomarker discovery, multi-omics and microbiome capabilities.

The company’s board approved the allotment of 21,883 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 13,118 per share to raise the aforesaid amount, according to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.

title: Apple Pay launches in India with Axis Bank cards; Razorpay, Cashfree and others enable merchant support
summary:
Apple has launched its Apple Pay payment service in India, with Axis Bank as its first banking partner. At launch, the service supports Visa and Mastercard credit cards issued by Axis Bank. The rollout allows iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users to make payments at contactless enabled stores, in apps and online. Mac support is expected soon.
The service is being enabled across merchant networks through payment infrastructure players including Razorpay and Cashfree, along with Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Juspay and Worldline.
Juspay said merchants on its network can add Apple Pay to their existing online payment flows without building a separate integration.
Cashfree has also enabled Apple Pay for its Indian business customers as part of the rollout. Apple said it has worked with Cashfree and other payment service providers to bring Apple Pay to their merchant networks in India.
Commenting on the launch, Amitabh Chaudhry, MD & CEO, Axis Bank, said, “We are at a significant inflection point in payments, where technology, intelligent security and changing customer expectations are reshaping how people transact. At Axis Bank, our aspiration is to remain at the forefront of this transformation by building payment experiences that are progressive, trusted and deeply relevant to our customers."
For in store payments, users can double click the side button on their iPhone, authenticate through Face ID, Touch ID or the device passcode and hold the device near a contactless payment terminal.
Apple Pay can also be used on supported apps and websites without requiring users to enter card details repeatedly. Users can add eligible cards through the Wallet app or the Axis Bank app.
At launch, Apple Pay will be accepted at millions of merchants across India, including Apple Store locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, Ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg and Zomato.
Apple Pay does not support UPI or RuPay cards at launch. The service is currently limited to eligible Visa and Mastercard credit cards issued by Axis Bank.
Apple Pay is available in more than 90 countries and regions and works with more than 11,000 bank and network partners globally.

summary:
Bengaluru- based edtech startup Arivihan has raised $10 million in Series A funding from existing investors Accel and Prosus Ventures, along with an additional $200,000 from its existing GSF angel investors.
The round takes the company’s total funding to more than $15 million.
Entrackr recently reported on the company’s new funding and estimated that its valuation had jumped 3.3X to around $60 million.
The fresh capital will be used to expand into new states and strengthen its presence in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Bihar. The company also plans to expand its CBSE offering, develop more vernacular language capabilities and increase its AI research efforts.
Founded in 2022 by Ritesh Singh Chandel, Sonu Kumar and Rushabh Kothari, Arivihan offers an AI based learning platform for school students. Its platform provides interactive video lessons, instant doubt solving and AI driven study plans without relying on live teachers.
The company currently serves students preparing for State Board, CBSE and NEET exams, with a focus on students from tier 2, tier 3 cities and rural areas. Arivihan said around 80% of its subscribers come from tier 3 cities and rural India.
Arivihan will also scale its digital marketing and on ground distribution network as it expands across India. The company plans to hire across key functions and launch new crash courses. Arivihan was previously part of Accel’s Atoms accelerator programme and received seed funding through the programme in March 2024.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Arivihan’s revenue jumped nearly 14.8X to Rs 3.14 crore from Rs 21.29 lakh in FY24, while the company posted a loss of Rs 4.45 crore.

title: Jedlik Motors founder Raguram SK on building electric pod for urban commuters
summary:
Chennai-based EV startup Jedlik Motors is developing a fully enclosed electric two wheeler, e-POD, aimed at combining the maneuverability of a scooter with the comfort and safety of a car.
In an interaction with Entrackr, Raguram SK, founder and CEO of Jedlik Motors, discussed the company’s product roadmap, business model, technology, funding plans and expansion strategy.
Raguram, a mechanical engineer by background, started his entrepreneurial journey with an online electric vehicle dealership in 2019. After the business was impacted by Covid 19, he worked as a mechanical designer at an MNC before starting Jedlik Motors.
The startup is currently at the MVP stage and has developed a prototype of the e-POD. According to Raguram, the company has secured two patents, of which one has been granted and another has been published.
The e-POD is designed for urban commuters who want protection from weather conditions without compromising on the maneuverability associated with two wheelers. The vehicle is expected to feature air conditioning, pushback seats, an infotainment system and around 600 litres of boot space.
The e-POD will also feature crab walking steering, which is designed to allow tighter turns and easier maneuverability in dense urban traffic.
“Essentially, we are developing a vehicle that combines the comfort and safety of a car with the maneuverability of a motorcycle,” Raguram said.
For consumers, Jedlik Motors is targeting an on road price of around Rs 2.5 lakh. The company is also exploring a battery as a service (BaaS) model, which could bring the upfront vehicle cost down to around Rs 1.5 lakh. The battery subscription is expected to cost approximately Rs 2,000 to Rs 2,500 per month, although the final pricing is still being worked out.
Jedlik Motors is also developing a separate B2B version of the vehicle for applications such as food delivery, quick commerce and large industrial campuses. The startup has initiated conversations with companies including Mahindra, Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland and Maruti Suzuki. It is also reaching out to Rapido, Yes Madam, Tiffit and Ajego.
On the technology front, the company is developing autonomous driving capabilities along with its own motors, controllers and steer by wire systems. The autonomous driving stack is being designed to eventually operate in increasingly complex traffic conditions.
The startup currently has a team of around 10 people and carries out assembly at its Chennai facility. Around 90% to 95% of its component designs are developed in house, while battery cells are currently sourced from Taiwan or China.
Jedlik Motors plans to launch the e-POD by June 2027, starting with a pilot in Bengaluru before expanding to Chennai and other tier 1 cities. It also plans to target markets such as the UAE and other Asian countries, with broader global expansion targeted by 2030.
The company has so far received around Rs 26 lakh in government grants and Rs 47 lakh in angel funding. It is currently looking to raise Rs 7 crore in a pre-seed round to support its next phase of development.

title: AceVector’s IPO subscribed over 5X on final day
summary:
AceVector, the parent company of Snapdeal, Unicommerce and Stellaro Brands, saw decent demand for its IPO, with the issue subscribed 5.07 times as investors bid for 36.61 crore shares against 7.22 crore shares on offer.
AceVector’s initial public offering (IPO) was open for subscription from September 25-September 29, with a price band of Rs 30-32 and a minimum investment of Rs 14,040 for a lot size of 468 shares.
According to exchange data, the non-institutional investors (NIIs) portion saw the highest demand with 8.53X subscription, followed by the retail quota at 4.83X, while the Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) portion was subscribed 3.42X.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 4.16 crore shares worth around Rs 133 crore at the upper price band.
SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners and other existing investors will partially offload their stakes through the OFS, while co-founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal will not sell any shares in the IPO.
The fresh proceeds from the IPO will primarily be used for Snapdeal’s marketing and business promotion, technology infrastructure, acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
Ahead of the IPO opening, AceVector raised Rs 189 crore from 14 anchor investors by allotting 5.91 crore shares at Rs 32 per share. The anchor book saw participation from Negen Undiscovered Value Fund, Singularity Growth Opportunities Fund, Turnaround Opportunities Fund, and mutual funds including Helios and Taurus.
AceVector’s operating revenue grew 29% to Rs 510.38 crore in FY26 from Rs 395.02 crore in FY25, while its adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to Rs 15.94 crore from Rs 39.16 crore.

title: ITC completes 100% acquisition of Yoga Bar parent Sproutlife
summary:
FMCG major ITC has completed the acquisition of Sproutlife Foods, the parent company of nutrition and healthy foods brand Yoga Bar, after acquiring the remaining stake in the Bengaluru based company.
According to its exchange filing, ITC acquired 13,445 equity shares of Sproutlife through a secondary purchase for around Rs 645 crore, increasing its shareholding from approximately 47.5% to 100%. Following the transaction, Sproutlife has become a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC effective September 28.
The acquisition was completed entirely through cash consideration. ITC said the acquisition is in line with its strategy to strengthen its future ready portfolio in the foods segment.
Sproutlife manufactures and sells food products under the Yoga Bar brand. Positioned as a digital first brand, Yoga Bar has a significant presence across D2C and e-commerce channels, along with a growing footprint in offline retail stores.
The company has recorded strong growth in recent years, with its turnover more than doubling to Rs 452 crore in FY26 from Rs 200 crore in FY25. Its turnover stood at Rs 108 crore in FY24.
ITC first invested in Yoga Bar parent Sproutlife Foods in May 2023, acquiring a 39.42% stake for Rs 175 crore, after announcing plans to acquire the company in phases in January that year. Since then, ITC gradually increased its holding to around 47.5%, before acquiring the remaining 52.5% stake in the latest transaction to complete the acquisition.
The deal comes amid a broader acquisition push by legacy FMCG companies to expand their presence in new age and digital first consumer brands. Besides Yoga Bar, ITC signed a deal in February 2025 to acquire Prasuma, which operates frozen and ready to cook food brands Prasuma and Meatigo, with plans to acquire 100% over three years. title: WEH Ventures announces first close of Fund III, targets Rs 250 Cr corpus
summary:
Seed stage venture capital firm WEH Ventures has announced the first close of Fund III, its third fund, with a target corpus of Rs 250 crore. The fund will back 20 to 25 early stage Indian startups serving customers in India and global markets.
WEH Ventures launched Fund I in 2017, followed by its flagship Fund II in 2020. Fund I has returned 1.4x capital, while Fund II has already returned capital through one exit and is tracking above top quartile performance, according to the firm.
The first close has attracted participation from family offices, exited founders and senior corporate and technology executives. Early backers include Play Capital, a Nordic fund of funds, and family offices such as Eraya, Twin & Bull Investments and Heritage Investments.
The investor base also includes exited founders from companies such as Oziva and GS Labs, along with senior executives and CEOs from Thermax, Haleon, Lenovo and PNB MetLife. Senior Silicon Valley executives associated with companies such as Arlo and Intuitive Surgical have also participated.
Fund III will invest across sectors such as advanced manufacturing, agriculture, energy transition, artificial intelligence and healthcare, along with consumer and fintech.
WEH Ventures has already started deploying capital from Fund III and has committed to eight investments across advanced agriculture, robotics, healthcare diagnostics, retail and edtech.
The fund's investments announced so far include Fragaria, which operates in advanced horticulture, Praan Health, which focuses on fitness services and health products, and PlayBlue, a sports retail company. One of its portfolio companies has also raised a subsequent round at a higher valuation.
WEH Ventures expects to complete the final close of Fund III by mid 2027.
Since 2017, the firm has invested in more than 30 companies. Its portfolio includes Smallcase, Jar, Pratilipi, Animall, MasterChow, AppsforBharat, Unbox Robotics and Mitigata.
The Indian startup ecosystem has seen several new seed and early stage funds in 2026, with investors focusing on sectors such as deeptech, AI, enterprise technology and IP led businesses.

title: Bewakoof’s revenue jumps 40% to Rs 243 Cr in FY26, losses rise 19%
summary:
Following a modest 7% growth in FY25, Aditya Birla Group-owned Bewakoof posted a strong 40% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in FY26. At the same time, the D2C fashion brand’s losses increased 19% during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Bewakoof’s operating revenue rose 40.5% to Rs 243 crore in FY26 from Rs 173 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).


Bewakoof is a lifestyle fashion brand that makes trendy products for contemporary India, including T-shirts, phone covers, bags and hoodies. Revenue from the sale of these products remained the company’s main source of income during the year.
On the cost side, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense for the company. It increased 45.7% to Rs 134 crore in FY26 from Rs 92 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses rose 7.7% to Rs 28 crore, while marketing expenses increased 26.5% to Rs 62 crore. Transportation and handling expenses, however, fell 17.1% to Rs 29 crore from Rs 35 crore.
Depreciation expenses jumped nearly three times to Rs 16.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 6 crore in FY25. Other expenses also increased 66.1% to Rs 66.4 crore from Rs 40 crore.
Overall, Bewakoof’s total expenses increased 35.5% to Rs 336 crore in FY26 from Rs 248 crore in the previous fiscal year.
As a result, the company’s loss widened 19.4% to Rs 87.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 73.2 crore in FY25, despite the strong growth in revenue.
However, some operating metrics improved. Bewakoof’s EBITDA loss narrowed slightly to Rs 59.8 crore from Rs 60.7 crore in FY25, while its EBITDA margin improved to -24.6% from -35.1%. The company’s return on capital employed (ROCE) also improved to -63.4% in FY26 from -96.6% in FY25.


At the unit level, Bewakoof spent Rs 1.38 to earn every Rs 1 of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.43 in the previous year.
Its total current assets stood at Rs 91.1 crore at the end of FY26, up from Rs 84.8 crore in FY25. Cash and bank balances increased slightly to Rs 22 lakh from Rs 18 lakh.
The strong revenue growth came in a year that also marked a leadership transition for Bewakoof.
Co-founder Prabhkiran Singh stepped down in February 2026 after 14 years with the company, a month before the end of FY26. Singh was therefore with the company for most of the fiscal year in which Bewakoof recorded 40% revenue growth.
The exit came three years after Aditya Birla Digital Fashion Ventures (ABDFVL) acquired a majority stake in Bewakoof in February 2023. ABDFVL is part of TMRW, the Aditya Birla Group’s digital-first fashion and lifestyle venture.

Founded in 2025, FIG Living started with lighting products such as table lamps, portable lamps, pendant lights, wall lights and floor lamps. The company has since expanded into side tables, accent furniture and tabletop products as it looks to build a broader home and lifestyle platform.

With the investment, FIG Living plans to expand its distribution network, strengthen physical brand experiences and add more consumer touchpoints. It will also explore global design partnerships and collaborations.

title: Peak XV unveils Surge 12 with 18 startups across AI, robotics, space, consumer, healthcare, music and fintech
summary:
Peak XV Partners has unveiled the 12th cohort of its seed stage programme Surge, comprising 18 early stage startups across artificial intelligence, robotics, space, consumer, healthcare, music and fintech.
The cohort includes Alma, August AI, Ditto, GameStock, hiloop, Hoola Health, Kello, Kindling, Puralink, Reinforce Labs, Riffle, Rosella, Tribe Money, ULOOK and Wingit, along with three startups that are currently in stealth mode.
Among the startups, Alma is building AI native personal computing infrastructure, while August AI is developing AI powered clinical intelligence for primary care. Ditto is working on an AI dating matchmaker inside iMessage, while GameStock is building a social and competitive layer for financial markets.
Hoola Health is building a paediatric care platform, while Kello is developing a people intelligence engine. Kindling is building a storytelling platform for technology startups and Reinforce Labs is focused on AI evaluation, red teaming and remediation for enterprises.
Puralink is developing autonomous robots for underground pipe infrastructure, while ULOOK is building RF sensing satellites for spectrum intelligence. Riffle is working on a browser based collaborative music platform, while Rosella is building an AI native commercial insurance brokerage.
Tribe Money is developing an AI based personal finance platform, while Wingit is building a beauty platform for premium consumers.
The cohort also includes founders with experience at companies such as Google, Airbnb, Microsoft Research, Sarvam AI and Reducto. Kello cofounder Mona Gandhi was Airbnb’s first female engineer, while Reinforce Labs founder Anish Das Sarma previously led AI and machine learning teams as a Director at Google.
Peak XV said the latest Surge cohort reflects a shift towards AI becoming the underlying architecture of products, alongside startups rebuilding familiar consumer experiences and applying technology to physical infrastructure.
Surge provides seed stage startups with up to $5 million in funding along with support across hiring, product, engineering, go to market, marketing, communications, policy and global expansion.
Since its launch in 2019, Surge has backed more than 180 startups across more than 18 nationalities. Its top 10 companies generate more than $1 billion in annual revenue, according to Peak XV.

title: Bharat Housing Network raises $5 Mn from Symbiotics
summary:
Bharat Housing Network (BHN), a secured credit network, has raised $5 million (around Rs 47 crore) in green bonds from Symbiotics. 
The bond is part of a $75 million green basket bond programme structured by Symbiotics with British International Investment (BII). 
BHN had previously raised Rs 125 crore ($14.5 million) in Series A funding led by NABVENTURES.
The capital will be deployed through BHN’s group NBFC, Singularity Creditworld, to finance green assets in India. The funds will support rooftop solar financing, electric mobility financing and credit for clean-tech MSMEs.
BHN claims its network has enabled nearly Rs 2,000 crore of credit to more than 40,000 low and middle-income borrowers. It has also financed 7,162 KW of rooftop solar capacity and more than 800 electric vehicles, with the financed assets having a potential to save around 1,01,500 tonnes of CO2 emissions.
Founded by Lalit Menghani, Madhusudan Sharma and Prasad Ajinkya, BHN is part of the Homeville Group. The company provides technology and infrastructure for capital deployment across mortgages, clean energy, mobility and gold loans. Its investors include NABVENTURES, 100Unicorns, Varanium, Riverwalk and LC Nueva.
BHN is also targeting up to $25 million in green bond issuances by the end of the next financial year. The proposed capital will be used to expand green asset financing and provide funding to sustainable businesses and retail borrowers across India.

The company may also consider a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 120 crore. If completed, the pre-IPO placement will reduce the size of the fresh issue. The company has proposed to list its equity shares on the BSE and NSE.
EverBrands operates Subway in India through Culinary Brands India Pvt Ltd (CBIPL). It also manages Lavazza Coffee and F&H Coffee and distributes Dilmah Tea in India through Fresh and Honest Cafe Pvt Ltd. The company operates Subway stores under both company-owned, company-operated (COCO) and franchisee-owned, franchisee-operated (FOFO) formats.
According to the DRHP, the company has appointed Motilal Oswal, ICICI Securities and Nuvama as book-running lead managers and MUFG as the registrar to the issue.
The company plans to use Rs 125 crore of the IPO proceeds to repay its borrowings. Another Rs 326.85 crore will be used for capital expenditure towards setting up new Subway stores under the COCO format, while the remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
For FY26, revenue for EverBrands grew 34.9% year-on-year to Rs 966.17 crore from Rs 716.06 crore in FY25. Its quick service restaurant (QSR) business, which includes Subway, contributed Rs 693.09 crore during the fiscal year, while the company’s loss widened to Rs 58.19 crore from Rs 28.26 crore in FY25. EBITDA stood at Rs 98.13 crore, compared with Rs 64.21 crore in the previous fiscal.
As of FY26, EverBrands had 678 COCO and 330 FOFO Subway stores in India, along with eight FOFO stores in Sri Lanka. Its Subway business accounted for nearly 72% of the company’s total operating revenue during the fiscal.
EverBrands Ventures Pte Ltd is the largest shareholder of the company with a 57.78% stake on a fully diluted basis, followed by Norwest Capital LLC with 16.48%. Shivanand Shankar Mankekar HUF holds 5.83%, while Playbook India Fund II owns 4.15%. Enrich Agro Food Products and Bikramjit Singh Kandhari each hold 3.64% in the company on a fully diluted basis.
Earlier this year, EverBrands raised $15 million in a funding round led by Playbook Partners. The investment reportedly involved a 5% stake in Subway India’s parent at a valuation of around Rs 2,600-2,800 crore. The IPO price band and issue dates have not been announced yet.

The round was co-led by Fidelity Management & Research Company and Amplify, with participation from Alter Venture Partners, Dell Technologies Capital and StepStone Group. AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital and J.P. Morgan also joined the round as new investors.
The proceeds will be used to scale Palette Neat, an agentic software environment for Physical AI, and develop next-generation hardware capable of delivering 1,000 TOPS of compute through purpose-built Physical AI silicon, SiMa.ai said in a press release.
Founded in 2018 by Krishna Rangasayee, SiMa.ai provides a software-centric platform for Physical AI applications. The company focuses on robotics, automotive, drones, industrial automation, aerospace and defence, smart vision and healthcare.
SiMa.ai said it serves more than 150 customers across automotive, drones and robotics, including ARK Electronics, AVerMedia, Bosch, Emerson, Intrinsic, Kontron, L&T Technology Services, Mistral, STIGA, Synopsys and Virya Autonomous Tech, among others.
According to market research cited by the company, the global Physical AI devices market, including robotics, automotive and drones, is projected to reach 145 million cumulative shipments by 2035.
SiMa.ai said Physical AI applications have traditionally relied on NVIDIA GPUs, which can be expensive and power intensive. The company offers a full-stack Physical AI platform that combines purpose-built silicon and software to simplify deployments.
Slated for H1 2028, the next-generation hardware will include machine learning IP, chiplets and SoCs. The company plans to target medium to high-end drones, humanoid robotics, automotive advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and AI-powered cockpits.

title: Ola Electric to raise up to Rs 1,000 Cr via rights issue
summary:
Electric two wheeler maker Ola Electric has approved a plan to raise up to Rs 1,000 crore through a rights issue of partly paid up equity shares.
The company’s board approved the proposal on September 28, subject to regulatory and statutory approvals. The issue will be open to eligible shareholders as of a record date, which will be announced later.
Ola Electric is yet to finalise the issue price, rights entitlement ratio, record date, issue timeline and payment terms. The number of shares to be issued will also be determined by the board.
The latest fundraise comes less than a month after Ola Electric approved a plan to raise up to Rs 1,500 crore through equity shares or convertible securities. The earlier fundraise could be carried out through a further public offer, rights issue, QIP, private placement or other permitted routes, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
In June, Ola Electric raised Rs 780 crore through a QIP by allotting around 21.76 crore shares at Rs 35.86 apiece to qualified institutional buyers.
Meanwhile, Ola Electric COO Hyun Shik Park resigned from his position effective September 5, citing personal reasons.
The fresh fundraise comes as the EV two wheeler maker faces pressure on market share, customer complaints and its stock performance. In Q1 FY27, its revenue from operations fell 45% year on year to Rs 455 crore, while its net loss narrowed to Rs 336 crore from Rs 428 crore a year earlier. The company recorded 13,170 vehicle registrations in July, giving it a 6.8% market share.
Ola Electric has also been scaling up its battery cell manufacturing operations. The company recently secured Rs 95.81 crore under the government’s PLI Auto scheme for FY27. The board has also approved increasing Ola Electric’s authorised share capital from Rs 8,318.5 crore to Rs 8,721.9 crore, subject to shareholder approval.

title: Moneyview IPO sees nearly 100X subscription on final day
summary:
Digital lending platform Moneyview’s IPO saw strong investor demand, with the issue subscribed 98.5X on the final day of bidding. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the demand, with their portion subscribed over 227X.
Moneyview’s initial public offering (IPO) was open for subscription from September 24-September 28, with a price band of Rs 32-34 and a minimum investment of Rs 14,112 for a lot size of 441 shares. 
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 750 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of up to 10.04 crore shares. At the upper price band, the issue is valued at around Rs 6,000 crore.
According to exchange data, the QIB portion was subscribed 227.5X, followed by non-institutional investors (NIIs) at 115.4X, while the retail portion saw 19.6X subscription.
Ahead of the IPO opening, Moneyview raised Rs 327.5 crore from anchor investors. The anchor book featured a mix of leading domestic mutual funds and global institutional investors including ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund Goldman Sachs, Amundi Funds, 360 ONE, HDFC Life and others.
The company plans to deploy Rs 325 crore from the fresh issue towards loan disbursals, while Rs 250 crore will be infused into its NBFC subsidiary, Whizdm Finance. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
Founded by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview offers financial products including personal loans, insurance, credit cards, and digital gold through its network of banks, NBFCs, insurers, and other financial institutions.
Financially, Moneyview reported revenue of Rs 3,351 crore and a profit of Rs 244 crore in FY26. In the June 2026 quarter, its revenue grew 50.2% year-on-year to Rs 1,041 crore, while profit surged 158.8% to Rs 173.8 crore.

title: Entrackr’s The Spur D2C Mixer brings together over 40 founders and 10 investors
summary:
What happens when you bring together over 40 D2C founders, 10 investors, cocktails and dinner, and take away the usual panels and presentations?
You get conversations that are far more real.
Entrackr hosted The Spur, D2C Mixer, presented by Entrackr and PhonePe Gateway, in Gurugram on September 25, bringing together founders, investors and leaders from the D2C ecosystem for an informal evening of conversations, connections and, of course, a lot of fun.
There were no panels, no presentations and no fixed agenda. The idea was simple: step away from work for a few hours and connect with people who are building in the same ecosystem.
And that is exactly what happened.
Founders spoke openly about what they are building, the challenges they are facing, what is working, what is not and the realities of building a consumer brand. Investors also joined these conversations, making the evening a space for candid discussions rather than the usual pitch-and-network format.
From business challenges and industry trends to founder journeys, the conversations moved freely through the evening. There was plenty of networking, new introductions, laughter and some brutally honest discussions that may not always happen in a formal setting.
For Entrackr, however, the evening was about something bigger than just one mixer.
The D2C ecosystem is growing rapidly, and there is a growing need for founders to have a space where they can connect, share experiences, learn from each other and simply be around people who understand the journey.
The Spur is our attempt to build that space.
This was a great start, but this is only the beginning. We plan to bring the community together through more such intimate gatherings across the D2C ecosystem.
More founders. More conversations. More connections. And hopefully, a strong D2C family along the way.

title: SC declines stay on UPI MDR rollout, seeks response from Centre, RBI, NPCI on plea
summary:
The Supreme Court has declined to stay the October 15 rollout of the new Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for specified UPI merchant transactions above Rs 2,000. The court has issued notices to the Centre, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on a plea challenging the framework.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the Centre, RBI and NPCI to file their responses within four weeks. The court also sought an explanation on the basis and legal character of the charge, according to Bar & Bench.
The plea, filed by advocate Anjan Datta, challenges the Centre's September 14 notification and the MDR framework announced on September 15. It questions the legal basis for imposing MDR on select UPI transactions and the manner in which the framework was introduced.
Under the new framework, a 0.4% MDR will apply to specified person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 and above. UPI payments to merchants of up to Rs 2,000 and person-to-person (P2P) transactions will continue to remain free.
Certain sectors, including railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, will attract a flat MDR of Rs 5 on transactions above Rs 2,000. Transactions involving mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers and dealers will carry an MDR of 0.02%, capped at Rs 300.
According to the Finance Ministry, the new framework will affect around 4% of merchant UPI transactions, leaving approximately 96% unaffected. The ministry has also clarified that MDR is neither a tax nor a charge collected by the government or NPCI, with the amount distributed among participants in the payments ecosystem.
The Finance Ministry has also said banks will ensure that merchants do not pass the MDR on to customers. The framework provides zero-MDR treatment to small merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month through UPI.
The new framework will end the zero-MDR regime for specified UPI merchant transactions that has been in place since 2020. The October 15 implementation remains in place following the Supreme Court's decision not to grant an interim stay.

summary:
Agricultural machinery company Balwaan Krishi has raised Rs 100 crore in a Series B funding round led by First Bridge India Growth Fund Private Equity, with participation from other institutional investors.
The Jaipur-based company had earlier raised $2 million in a pre-Series A round led by Caspian Leap for Agriculture Fund, with participation from angels including Deepak Agarwal, Rishab Jain and Pulkit Bachhawat in May 2023.
The fresh capital will be used to expand domestic manufacturing capacity, strengthen dealer and service networks in Southern India, and develop farm equipment with predictive maintenance and IoT capabilities, Balwaan Krishi said in a press release.
Founded in 2016 by Rohit Bajaj and Shubham Bajaj, Balwaan Krishi makes agricultural equipment for Indian farming conditions. The company has more than 800 dealers across Northern India, along with an e-commerce presence, and serves over four lakh farmers across the country.
Balwaan Krishi said around 86% of Indian farmers are small and marginal farmers cultivating less than two hectares. Its product portfolio is priced between Rs 10,000 and Rs 1 lakh, targeting this segment through a hybrid B2B and B2C distribution model.
The company plans to expand its manufacturing capabilities in India to improve control over product quality, supply chains and availability, while reducing dependence on imported machinery and components. It also plans to expand its presence in Southern India, with a focus on product availability and after-sales service.
The agricultural machinery startup ecosystem has seen growing activity across electric tractors, robotics, AI, automation and digital platforms.
In 2025, electric tractor startup Moonrider raised $6 million from Pi Ventures and Singularity AMC after an earlier $2.2 million seed round. Harvested Robotics raised Rs 5 crore in seed funding from Arali Ventures, with participation from Anand Mahindra and others, to develop AI-powered laser weeding technology for tractors.
Tractor Junction, a digital marketplace for tractors and agricultural equipment, raised $22.6 million in Series A funding led by Astanor, with participation from Info Edge and Omnivore.
